one_month_reasoning: The window runs from 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-30. The Q3 2026 report is estimated for Nov 3, but that date is not confirmed (src 21). Eaton reported Q3 on Oct 31 in 2023 and 2024 (src 25), so I put about 25-30% odds on a print inside the window. Management said at Laguna on Sep 16 that Q3 was 'very strong' and tracking to the high end of guidance (src 19). An in-window print is therefore slightly positive on the headline, but the Q4 margin guide and the 2027 framing add two-way variance. The other in-window events are also two-sided: the Oct 27-28 FOMC, after a September hike with the 10-year at 5.24% (src 20); hyperscaler Q3 capex commentary; and peer prints from VRT, GEV and Schneider. Short interest is about 1.9% of float, too small to matter (src 9). I use a lognormal with its median at about $433.5 (tiny drift) and 11% monthly vol (39%/3.5), a touch wider than round 1 because of the possible earnings print, with a slightly fatter far-left tail.

fair_value.method: Blend of 60% forward P/E ($413 = skeptic pro-forma ex-Mobility NTM EPS at Sep 2027 of $16.53 x 25x) and 40% FCF yield ($432 = NTM FCF of $5.11B on ~381.5M post-split-off shares = $13.4/share at a 3.1% yield). Both legs now use a pro-forma, ex-Mobility base with ~8M shares retired, and the 25x multiple reflects a verified 5.24% 10-year.

inputs_detail.input: FY2027 consensus EPS (includes a full year of Mobility)

inputs_detail.value: Exchange offer retiring ~8M ETN shares; ~$1.1B cash to Eaton for capital allocation including debt repayment; close Q1 2027
inputs_detail.derivation: The share count (~8M) is an estimate: SpinCo equity worth roughly $3.5B, exchanged at about the ETN price, retires about 8M shares. This matches the supervisor's figure.

Consensus about $15.7 less about 3% net split-off dilution (about $350M/yr of lost after-tax Mobility profit, partly offset by ~8M retired shares and ~$40M of interest saved) gives about $15.2. I take off about 0.7% more for price/cost and ramp risk (src 23, 6). That haircut is smaller than in round 1 because Laguna says Q3 is tracking to the high end (src 19).

The pro-forma 2027 base of $15.2 grown about 14%, in line with consensus growth to 2028 (the UBS-derived 2028 consensus of $18.64 is only one data point, src 7), gives $17.35. I trim about 2% for Boyd's low initial returns and a possible slowdown in data-center order growth as hyperscaler capex growth slows in 2028 (src 11, 12).

The stock trades at about 27.5x 2027 consensus and 31x 2026 EPS (src 6). The 10-year is 5.24% and the Fed hiked on Sep 17 (src 20), which argues against any re-rating (src 4). Trefis notes the multiple is near its 10-year high (src 23). A year from now, with the runway one year shorter, I hold 25x. Laguna lowers Q3 execution risk, but the verified rate headwind offsets that, so the multiple is unchanged from round 1. I no longer lean on the Simply Wall St DCF (src 5).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF at Sep-2027 = 0.25 x 2027E $4.55B + 0.75 x 2028E $5.3B = $5.11B / 381.5M shares = $13.4/share; at a 3.1% FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: LTM $4.0B grown about 20% (Q2 FCF +22%) gives about $4.8B. Less about $0.25B for three quarters without Mobility (Q2 operating profit $109M/quarter, src 17/1), net of the interest saved from the $1.1B debt paydown.
About 16% growth on 2027, in line with EPS growth plus lower interest as net debt falls from about $19.9B toward $17-18B (src 18).
389.5M (Q2) less about 8M retired in the exchange offer. No buybacks in 2026 per the 10-Q (src 18), and I assume none of consequence before the horizon.

The current yield is about 2.4%. Leverage (net debt about $19.9B) argues for some de-rating toward 3%, and the 10-year at 5.24% argues for a bit more. Against that, Moody's affirmed A3 stable after the Boyd announcement (src 22), so the credit tail is contained. Hence 3.1%, not higher.

bear.story: Hyperscalers signal capex digestion in 2027-28 (src 11, 12), Electrical Americas rolling orders turn negative on tough comparisons, and the price/cost recovery stalls (src 23). Pro-forma 2028 EPS falls to about $15.5 and, with the 10-year above 5%, the multiple drops to about 19-20x: about $300. No buybacks until 2027 and about $18B net debt limit the support.

base.story: Q3 lands at the high end as management signalled (src 19). Data-center and utility demand holds through 2027, the Mobility split-off closes in Q1 2027 (about 3% EPS dilution, ~8M shares retired, $1.1B to debt), and pro-forma NTM EPS reaches about $16.5-16.8 at 25-26x. The stock ends roughly flat.

bull.story: The UBS-style case: segment margins step up as guided, price/cost turns into a tailwind in 2027, 2028 pro-forma EPS is about $19-20, and the AI-power scarcity story holds about 28-29x despite high rates: about $570.

thesis_break_reason: Around $320 the stock would sit near its $312 52-week low and at about 19-20x skeptic pro-forma NTM EPS of about $16.5. A rate-driven de-rating alone (10-year above 5%) could plausibly take ETN to the mid-$300s, so I only treat $320 as a break if order data confirm it: a negative Electrical Americas rolling-order print, data-center order cancellations or deferrals, or a failed H2 2026 margin step-up at the Q3/Q4 reports. I raised the level from $300 because by $300 an order break would already be priced. I stay below the supervisor's $330 because the rate backdrop means a non-fundamental drawdown can reach the low-to-mid $300s (the stock fell 16% in the 2024 selloff, src 23, and 7.6% in a day in September).

reasoning: Round 2 incorporates the supervisor's verified facts. (1) The Mobility/Dana deal is a split-off by exchange offer (confirmed in the Form 425, src 17). It retires ~8M ETN shares and sends $1.1B to debt repayment, so round 1 was wrong to hold shares flat at 389.5M. I rebuilt both legs on a pro-forma ex-Mobility base (net ~3% EPS dilution) with ~381.5M shares, and dropped my separate 4% Mobility/interest haircut so it is not double-counted. (2) Management said at Laguna that Q3 is 'very strong' and at the high end (src 19), so I cut my extra execution haircut to under 1% on 2027. (3) The 10-year at 5.24% and the Sep 17 Fed hike are verified (src 20). They keep my multiple at 25x NTM, below the supervisor's 26x, and support a fat left tail. (4) I no longer rely on the Simply Wall St DCF, and I treat the 2028 UBS-derived consensus as a single data point. New skeptic-lane checks: Moody's affirmed A3 with a stable outlook after the Boyd announcement (src 22), so credit is not a live tail risk, which lifts the far-left ladder slightly. No September downgrade was found; Wells Fargo initiated at Overweight with a $503 target (src 24). Trefis flags Electrical Americas price/cost and a near-record multiple (src 23). There is still no short report, accounting flag or material litigation. Fair value is $421 (P/E $413 x 0.6 + FCF $432 x 0.4), about 3% below spot and little changed from $419 because the corrections offset: share retirement and a smaller execution haircut add value, a lower pro-forma EPS base and higher rates take it away. The scenarios (bear $300 at 22%, base $437 at 53%, bull $570 at 25%) give a mean of about $439 including drift. The ladder is a lognormal with its median near $430 and about 34% vol with a fatter left tail, so P(>= spot) is 0.49. Research this round was 5 searches and fetches, and the S&P post-Boyd rating was still not found.
